changes.before: God also said to Moses, “Say this to the sons of Israel: ‘YHWH, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.’ This is My name forever, the name by which I am to be remembered from generation to generation.
changes.after: God also said to Moses, “Say this to the sons of Israel: ‘YHWH, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.’ This is My name forever, and this is how I am to be remembered from generation to generation.
changes.reason: The Hebrew sets two parallel clauses, zeh shemi … ve-zeh zikhri (“this is My name … and this is My remembrance”); restoring the second “this” keeps the parallel, and “how I am to be remembered” follows Rashi (He taught Moses how the Name is to be called).

changes.before: Moses said to YHWH, “Please, my Lord, I have never been a man of words, neither before nor since You spoke to Your servant, for I am heavy of mouth and heavy of tongue.”
changes.after: Moses said to YHWH, “Please, my Lord, I am not a man of words, not yesterday, not the day before, and not since You spoke to Your servant, for I am heavy of mouth and heavy of tongue.”
changes.reason: The Hebrew says “I am not a man of words” and repeats gam three times (“yesterday … the day before … since You spoke”), words Rashi counts to show Moses held back for seven days at the bush; “neither before nor since” dropped them.

changes.before: YHWH did this the next day. All Egypt’s livestock died, but not one of the sons of Israel’s livestock died.
changes.after: YHWH did this the next day. All Egypt’s livestock died, but of the livestock of the sons of Israel not one died.
changes.reason: Aloud, “not one of the sons of Israel’s livestock” first sounds like “not one of the sons”; following the Hebrew order (“of the livestock of the sons of Israel not one died”) removes the slip.

changes.before: “and so that you may tell your son and your son’s son how I dealt harshly with the Egyptians and what signs I performed among them, and you may know that I am YHWH.”
changes.after: “and so that you may tell your son and your son’s son how I made a mockery of the Egyptians and what signs I performed among them, and you may know that I am YHWH.”
changes.reason: Rashi reads hit’allalti as “I made sport of” (as in Balaam’s “you have made a mockery of me,” Numbers 22:29), not a word for deeds; “dealt harshly” lost that image.

changes.before: “You shall observe the Unleavened Bread, for on this very day I brought your hosts out of the land of Egypt. You shall observe this day throughout your generations as a perpetual statute.
changes.after: “You shall guard the unleavened bread, for on this very day I brought your hosts out of the land of Egypt. You shall observe this day throughout your generations as a perpetual statute.
changes.reason: The Hebrew has no word for “feast” here; Rashi, with Onkelos, reads ushmartem et-hamatzot as guarding the unleavened bread so that it does not become leavened, which the festival name “the Unleavened Bread” obscured.

changes.before: The time the sons of Israel lived in Egypt was four hundred and thirty years.
changes.after: The dwelling of the sons of Israel, who dwelt in Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years.
changes.reason: Rashi shows the 430 years cannot all have been spent in Egypt (they are counted from the covenant between the pieces) and reads “who dwelt in Egypt” as describing the people; the previous wording placed the whole span in Egypt.

changes.before: When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them by the road through the land of the Philistines, although it was near. For God said, “The people may change their minds when they see war and return to Egypt.”
changes.after: When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them by the road through the land of the Philistines, because it was near. For God said, “The people may change their minds when they see war and return to Egypt.”
changes.reason: Rashi reads ki karov hu as the reason, not a concession: the road was near, so it would be easy to turn back to Egypt, as the following clause explains.

changes.before: He removed their chariot wheels and made them move with difficulty. The Egyptians said, “Let us flee from Israel, for YHWH is fighting for them against the Egyptians.”
changes.after: He removed their chariot wheels and made them drive heavily. The Egyptians said, “Let us flee from Israel, for YHWH is fighting for them against the Egyptians.”
changes.reason: Bikhvedut (“heavily”) is the word of Pharaoh’s heavy heart, and Rashi notes the measure for measure: as they made their hearts heavy, so He made them drive heavily; “with difficulty” lost the link.

changes.before: “You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain of Your inheritance, the place You made for Your dwelling, YHWH, the sanctuary Your hands established, Lord.
changes.after: “You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain of Your inheritance, the place You made for Your dwelling, YHWH, the sanctuary, Lord, that Your hands established.
changes.reason: Following the Hebrew order (mikdash Adonai), the vocative “Lord” now stands after “the sanctuary,” in parallel with “YHWH” in the line before; at the end of the verse it sounded tacked on to “established.”

changes.before: “I have heard the sons of Israel’s grumbling. Tell them: Between the evenings you shall eat meat, and in the morning you shall have your fill of bread. You shall know that I am YHWH your God.”
changes.after: “I have heard the grumbling of the sons of Israel. Tell them: Between the evenings you shall eat meat, and in the morning you shall have your fill of bread. You shall know that I am YHWH your God.”
changes.reason: “The sons of Israel’s grumbling” is awkward aloud; the of-phrase follows the Hebrew word order and the column’s usual wording.

changes.before: The house of Israel called it Man. It was like coriander seed, white, and tasted like wafers with honey.
changes.after: The house of Israel called it manna. It was like coriander seed, white, and tasted like wafers with honey.
changes.reason: Aloud, “called it Man” sounds like the English word “man”; “manna,” the form the column uses in 16:33 and 16:35, names the same Hebrew word without the confusion.

changes.before: In the third month after the sons of Israel left the land of Egypt, on that day they came to the wilderness of Sinai.
changes.after: In the third month after the sons of Israel left the land of Egypt, on this day they came to the wilderness of Sinai.
changes.reason: The Hebrew is בַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה, “on this day,” not “on that day”; Rashi stresses the “this” (the words of Torah should be as new to you as if given today).

changes.before: YHWH said to Moses, “Behold, I am coming to you in a thick cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you and trust you forever.” Moses told the people’s words to YHWH.
changes.after: YHWH said to Moses, “Behold, I am coming to you in a thick cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you, and may also trust you forever.” Moses told the people’s words to YHWH.
changes.reason: Restores וְגַם (“and also”), on which Rashi comments (also the prophets who come after you).

changes.before: “‘No hand shall touch him, but he shall surely be stoned or shot. Whether animal or human, he shall not live. When the ram’s horn sounds a long blast, they may go up the mountain.’”
changes.after: “‘No hand shall touch him, but he shall surely be stoned or thrown down. Whether animal or human, he shall not live. When the ram’s horn sounds a long blast, they may go up the mountain.’”
changes.reason: יָרֹה יִיָּרֶה can mean “shot” or “cast down”; Rashi reads it as being thrown down to the ground (as יָרָה in 15:4), so “shot” follows a reading the edition does not prefer.

changes.before: He said to the people, “Be ready for the third day. Do not approach a woman.”
changes.after: He said to the people, “Be ready for three days. Do not approach a woman.”
changes.reason: Moses says לִשְׁלֹשֶׁת יָמִים, “for three days,” not the “for the third day” of 19:11; Rashi builds on the difference, so it should not be harmonised.

changes.before: If it was torn by a wild animal, he shall bring it as evidence. He shall not make restitution for what was torn.
changes.after: If it was torn by a wild animal, he shall bring witnesses. He shall not make restitution for what was torn.
changes.reason: יְבִאֵהוּ עֵד is ambiguous (bring the carcass as evidence, or bring a witness); Onkelos (ייתי ליה סהדין) and Rashi read “let him bring witnesses that it was torn,” which the edition follows.

changes.before: You shall not spread a false report. Do not join hands with a wicked person to be a malicious witness.
changes.after: You shall not accept a false report. Do not join hands with a wicked person to be a malicious witness.
changes.reason: לֹא תִשָּׂא can mean “take up” or “carry”; Onkelos (לא תקבל) and Rashi read it as a warning not to accept a false report (and for a judge not to hear one side alone), not to spread one.

changes.before: and they saw the God of Israel. Under His feet was something like a pavement of sapphire, clear as the very heavens.
changes.after: and they saw the God of Israel. Under His feet was something like the work of a sapphire brick, clear as the very heavens.
changes.reason: כְּמַעֲשֵׂה לִבְנַת הַסַּפִּיר is “like the work of a brick of sapphire”; Rashi explains the brick as a reminder of Israel’s slavery in brickwork, an image “pavement” loses.

changes.before: You shall cast four gold rings for it and place them on its four feet, two rings on one side and two on the other.
changes.after: You shall cast four gold rings for it and place them on its four corners, two rings on one side and two on the other.
changes.reason: פַּעֲמֹתָיו is ambiguous (feet or corners); Onkelos (זויתיה) and Rashi read “its corners,” the upper corners next to the cover.

changes.before: See that you make them according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain.
changes.after: See, and make them according to their pattern, which you are being shown on the mountain.
changes.reason: וּרְאֵה וַעֲשֵׂה are two commands, “see and make,” with the participle מָרְאֶה (“being shown”); Rashi reads it as God showing Moses the model there on the mountain, which “see that you make” loses.

changes.before: When they enter the Tent of Meeting, they shall wash with water so that they do not die, and when they approach the altar to minister and burn an offering by fire to YHWH.
changes.after: When they enter the Tent of Meeting, or when they approach the altar to minister and burn an offering by fire to YHWH, they shall wash with water so that they do not die.
changes.reason: Read aloud, the closing “and when they approach the altar…” is left without a main clause; placing both occasions (joined by אוֹ, “or”) before the washing makes clear the command covers each.

changes.before: YHWH said to Moses, “Take fragrant spices: stacte, onycha, galbanum, and pure frankincense, in equal portions.
changes.after: YHWH said to Moses, “Take fragrant spices—stacte, onycha, and galbanum—fragrant spices and pure frankincense, in equal portions.
changes.reason: The Hebrew repeats סַמִּים (“spices”) before the frankincense; Rashi, following Keritot 6b, derives further incense spices from the repetition, so it is kept.

changes.before: Make them into incense, a perfumer’s compound, salted, pure, and holy.
changes.after: Make them into incense, a perfumer’s compound, well blended, pure, and holy.
changes.reason: מְמֻלָּח is ambiguous; Onkelos (מערב) and Rashi read it as “thoroughly mixed” (like sailors stirring the water with oars) rather than “salted.”

changes.before: “Tell the sons of Israel: ‘You must keep My Sabbaths, for they are a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, so that you may know that I am YHWH who sanctifies you.
changes.after: “Tell the sons of Israel: ‘Nevertheless, you must keep My Sabbaths, for they are a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, so that you may know that I am YHWH who sanctifies you.
changes.reason: Restores the limiting particle אַךְ; Rashi reads it as “even though you are eager in the work of the tabernacle, it shall not override the Sabbath,” linking the command to the craft instructions before it.

changes.before: So I told them, ‘Whoever has gold, take it off.’ They gave it to me, I threw it into the fire, and this calf came out.”
changes.after: So I said to them, ‘Who has gold?’ They took it off and gave it to me. I threw it into the fire, and this calf came out.”
changes.reason: הִתְפָּרָקוּ can be read as a command or as narrative; Rashi reads Aaron as saying only “Who has gold?” while the people hurried to take it off and give it, the edition’s Rabbinic-priority reading.

changes.before: YHWH had said to Moses, “Tell the sons of Israel: ‘You are a stiff-necked people. If I go up among you for a moment, I may consume you. Now remove your ornaments, so that I may know what to do with you.’”
changes.after: YHWH said to Moses, “Tell the sons of Israel: ‘You are a stiff-necked people. If I go up among you for a moment, I may consume you. Now remove your ornaments, so that I may know what to do with you.’”
changes.reason: וַיֹּאמֶר is a plain sequential verb; the pluperfect “had said” places God’s words before the mourning of 33:4, whereas Rashi reads “and now remove your ornaments” as a new penalty given at this point.

changes.before: The sons of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Horeb onward.
changes.after: The sons of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Horeb.
changes.reason: מֵהַר חוֹרֵב is ambiguous; Rashi reads it as the ornaments they had received at Mount Horeb, while “onward” adds a time span the Hebrew does not state.

changes.before: He said, “If I have found favor in Your sight, my Lord, please go among us, though this is a stiff-necked people. Pardon our iniquity and sin, and take us as Your inheritance.”
changes.after: He said, “If I have found favor in Your sight, my Lord, please let my Lord go among us, though this is a stiff-necked people. Pardon our iniquity and sin, and take us as Your inheritance.”
changes.reason: The Hebrew repeats אֲדֹנָי as the subject of יֵלֶךְ־נָא (“let my Lord, please, go among us”), Moses’ deferential answer to 33:3 (“I will not go up among you”); the repeated title had been dropped.

changes.before: He shall remove its crop with its feathers and throw it beside the altar on the east, at the place for ashes.
changes.after: He shall remove its crop with its contents and throw it beside the altar on the east, at the place for ashes.
changes.reason: בְּנֹצָתָהּ is ambiguous; Onkelos (בְּאוּכְלֵיהּ, “with its food”) and Rashi (“with its innards”) read it as what the crop holds, not the bird’s feathers.

changes.before: He shall bring it to Aaron’s sons, the priests, and take from it a full handful of its fine flour and oil, with all its frankincense. The priest shall burn its memorial portion on the altar: an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to YHWH.
changes.after: He shall bring it to Aaron’s sons, the priests, and the priest shall take from it a full handful of its fine flour and oil, with all its frankincense. The priest shall burn its memorial portion on the altar: an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to YHWH.
changes.reason: The subject of וְקָמַץ is unstated; Rashi (the scooping may be done where a non-priest stands) takes it as the priest, as 5:12 says outright, whereas the English had the lay offerer take the handful.

changes.before: or his sin that he has committed is made known to him, he shall bring as his offering an unblemished male goat.
changes.after: once his sin that he has committed is made known to him, he shall bring as his offering an unblemished male goat.
changes.reason: Rashi reads אוֹ הוֹדַע as אִם הוֹדַע (“if/when it is made known”): the leader brings his offering once he learns of the sin, as in 4:14; “or” made being informed a separate trigger.

changes.before: or his sin that he has committed is made known to him, he shall bring as his offering an unblemished female goat for the sin he has committed.
changes.after: when his sin that he has committed is made known to him, he shall bring as his offering an unblemished female goat for the sin he has committed.
changes.reason: As in 4:23, Rashi reads אוֹ הוֹדַע as “if/when it is made known”, matching “when the sin … becomes known” in 4:14; “or” made being informed a separate trigger.

changes.before: or anything about which he swore falsely. He shall repay its principal and add a fifth to it. He shall give it to its owner on the day of his guilt offering.
changes.after: or anything about which he swore falsely. He shall repay its principal and add a fifth to it. He shall give it to its owner on the day he acknowledges his guilt.
changes.reason: בְּיוֹם אַשְׁמָתוֹ is “the day of his guilt” (אַשְׁמָה), not of his guilt offering (אָשָׁם); Rashi explains it as the day he admits his guilt, before the offering of 5:25.

changes.before: With cakes of leavened bread he shall present his offering, with his sacrifice of thanksgiving and well-being.
changes.after: With cakes of leavened bread he shall present his offering, with his thanksgiving sacrifice of well-being.
changes.reason: זֶבַח תּוֹדַת שְׁלָמָיו is one sacrifice, the thanksgiving kind of well-being offering, rendered “his thanksgiving sacrifice of well-being” in 7:15; “thanksgiving and well-being” sounds like two sacrifices.

changes.before: For I am YHWH who brings you up from the land of Egypt to be your God. You shall be holy, for I am holy.
changes.after: For I am YHWH who brought you up from the land of Egypt to be your God. You shall be holy, for I am holy.
changes.reason: The participle הַמַּעֲלֶה refers here to the completed Exodus (Rashi paraphrases it as הֶעֱלֵיתִי, “I brought you up”), and the column renders the same construction as past in 22:33; present “brings” sounds aloud as if Israel were still leaving Egypt.

changes.before: On the seventh day the priest shall examine him. If the lesion remains unchanged in his eyes and has not spread in the skin, the priest shall isolate him for another seven days.
changes.after: On the seventh day the priest shall examine him. If the lesion remains unchanged in its appearance and has not spread in the skin, the priest shall isolate him for another seven days.
changes.reason: עָמַד בְּעֵינָיו means the lesion kept its own appearance (Rashi: “in its appearance and its original size”; cf. עֵינוֹ in 13:55), not anyone’s eyes; “in his eyes” points the listener to the man or the priest.

changes.before: But if in his eyes the scaly lesion has remained unchanged and black hair has grown in it, the scaly lesion has healed. He is clean, and the priest shall declare him clean.
changes.after: But if the scaly lesion has remained unchanged in its appearance and black hair has grown in it, the scaly lesion has healed. He is clean, and the priest shall declare him clean.
changes.reason: As in 13:5, בְּעֵינָיו refers to the lesion’s own appearance (Rashi), so “in his eyes” misleads; the order is adjusted so the phrase attaches to the lesion.

changes.before: The goat shall bear upon itself all their iniquities to a remote land, and he shall release the goat in the wilderness.
changes.after: The goat shall bear upon itself all their iniquities to a land cut off, and he shall release the goat in the wilderness.
changes.reason: אֶרֶץ גְּזֵרָה is literally a land “cut off” (Rashi: מְנֻתֶּקֶת, severed); “remote” loses the source’s image of the iniquities being carried to a land cut off from the people.

changes.before: For the life of all flesh is its blood with its life. I said to the sons of Israel: You shall not eat the blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood. Whoever eats it shall be cut off.
changes.after: For the life of all flesh—its blood is bound up with its life. I said to the sons of Israel: You shall not eat the blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood. Whoever eats it shall be cut off.
changes.reason: “Is its blood with its life” does not parse aloud; Rashi explains דָּמוֹ בְנַפְשׁוֹ הוּא as the life depending on the blood, which “bound up with” conveys while keeping the verse’s two distinct statements.

changes.before: If a man lies with a woman during her menstrual illness and uncovers her nakedness, he has exposed her fountain, and she has uncovered the source of her blood. Both shall be cut off from among their people.
changes.after: If a man lies with a woman during her menstrual illness and uncovers her nakedness, he has exposed her source, and she has uncovered the source of her blood. Both shall be cut off from among their people.
changes.reason: The Hebrew uses מְקוֹר twice (מְקֹרָהּ … מְקוֹר דָּמֶיהָ); “source” restores the deliberate repetition and matches “the source of her blood” in 12:7.

changes.before: As the years increase, you shall increase its purchase price; as the years decrease, you shall decrease its purchase price, for he is selling you a number of harvests.
changes.after: When the years are many, you shall increase its purchase price; when the years are few, you shall decrease its purchase price, for he is selling you a number of harvests.
changes.reason: לְפִי רֹב הַשָּׁנִים / מְעֹט הַשָּׁנִים means “according to many / few years”; “as the years increase” sounds aloud like the passing of time, which would reverse the sense (fewer harvests remain as time passes).

changes.before: If your brother becomes poor and his hand falters beside you, you shall support him as a resident foreigner and a lodger, so that he may live with you.
changes.after: If your brother becomes poor and his hand falters beside you, you shall support him, even if he is a resident foreigner or a lodger, so that he may live with you.
changes.reason: גֵּר וְתוֹשָׁב stands without “as” and is ambiguous; following Rashi (“even if he is a ger or a toshav”) the duty of support extends to them, rather than treating the poor brother as a foreigner.

changes.before: Those of you who remain will waste away in your enemies’ lands because of their own guilt. They will also waste away with their fathers because of their fathers’ guilt.
changes.after: Those of you who remain will waste away in your enemies’ lands because of their own guilt. They will also waste away because of their fathers’ guilt, which is with them.
changes.reason: אִתָּם refers to the fathers’ iniquities still with them (Rashi and Onkelos: the fathers’ deeds they hold in their hands), not to the fathers wasting away alongside them.

changes.before: Nadab and Abihu died before YHWH when they offered unauthorized fire before YHWH in the wilderness of Sinai. They had no sons. Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests in the presence of Aaron their father.
changes.after: Nadab and Abihu died before YHWH when they offered unauthorized fire before YHWH in the wilderness of Sinai. They had no sons. Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests during the lifetime of Aaron their father.
changes.reason: עַל־פְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן is read by Rashi as “in Aaron’s lifetime” (as at Genesis 11:28 in the previous pass); “in the presence of” suggests only that he was watching.

changes.before: They must not enter to see the holy things as they are covered, lest they die.
changes.after: They must not enter to see while the holy things are being covered, lest they die.
changes.reason: כְּבַלַּע is the moment of wrapping (Rashi: as the holy things are put into their coverings); “as they are covered” can be heard as “in their covered state,” which would forbid the Kohathites the very things they carry.

changes.before: YHWH said to Moses, saying:
changes.after: YHWH said to Moses:
changes.reason: “Said … saying” trips the ear; לֵאמֹר after וַיֹּאמֶר only introduces the speech, and the column renders the same formula “YHWH said to Moses:” elsewhere in Numbers.

changes.before: Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ relative by marriage: We are setting out for the place of which YHWH said, “I will give it to you.” Come with us, and we will treat you well, for YHWH has promised good for Israel.
changes.after: Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law: We are setting out for the place of which YHWH said, “I will give it to you.” Come with us, and we will treat you well, for YHWH has promised good for Israel.
changes.reason: חֹתֵן מֹשֶׁה is rendered “Moses’ father-in-law” throughout Exodus in this column, and Rashi identifies Hobab with Jethro; “relative by marriage” blurs the relationship the Hebrew names.

changes.before: The people were like those complaining of hardship in YHWH’s hearing. YHWH heard, and His anger flared; fire from YHWH burned among them and consumed the edge of the camp.
changes.after: The people were like those who complain, and it was evil in YHWH’s hearing. YHWH heard, and His anger flared; fire from YHWH burned among them and consumed the edge of the camp.
changes.reason: רַע בְּאָזְנֵי יְהוָה is ambiguous; following Rashi (a complaint that was evil in YHWH’s ears) and Onkelos, רַע describes the complaint, not a hardship being complained of.

changes.before: But as I live, and as YHWH’s glory fills all the earth,
changes.after: But as I live, and as YHWH’s glory shall fill all the earth,
changes.reason: וְיִמָּלֵא is future (Rashi: “and My glory will fill all the earth”); present “fills” turns the oath’s promise into a statement of fact.

changes.before: YHWH said to Moses, saying,
changes.after: YHWH said to Moses,
changes.reason: “Said … saying” trips the ear; לֵּאמֹר after וַיֹּאמֶר only introduces the speech, as already changed at Numbers 7:4, and this section renders וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוָה אֶל־מֹשֶׁה as “YHWH said to Moses,” (15:35).

changes.before: Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, took action, with Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, descendants of Reuben.
changes.after: Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, separated himself, with Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, descendants of Reuben.
changes.reason: וַיִּקַּח has no object; Rashi (he took himself to one side to break away from the congregation) and Onkelos (וְאִתְפְּלֵג) read it as Korah separating himself, which “took action” does not convey.

changes.before: YHWH spoke to Aaron: Look, I have given you charge of My contributions, all the holy gifts of the sons of Israel. I have given them to you as an allotted portion, and to your sons as a perpetual statute.
changes.after: YHWH spoke to Aaron: Look, I have given you charge of My contributions, all the holy gifts of the sons of Israel. I have given them to you as an anointed portion, and to your sons as a perpetual statute.
changes.reason: לְמָשְׁחָה is the anointing word of מִשְׁחַת in Leviticus 7:35, which the column renders “anointed portion” (Rashi on both: a portion given as a mark of greatness); “allotted portion” loses the image.

changes.before: For the unclean person they shall take some ashes from the burned purification offering, and fresh water shall be put over them in a vessel.
changes.after: For the unclean person they shall take some ashes from the burned purification offering, and living water shall be put over them in a vessel.
changes.reason: מַיִם חַיִּים is rendered “living water” in Leviticus 14–15 in this column; “fresh water” loses the source’s image and the link to those purification rites.

changes.before: YHWH said to Moses and Aaron: Because you did not trust Me to show Me holy before the eyes of the sons of Israel, you shall not bring this assembly into the land that I have given them.
changes.after: YHWH said to Moses and Aaron: Because you did not trust Me, and so did not show Me holy before the eyes of the sons of Israel, you shall not bring this assembly into the land that I have given them.
changes.reason: “Trust Me to show Me holy” is heard as God being trusted to do the sanctifying; in לְהַקְדִּישֵׁנִי the failure to sanctify is Moses’ and Aaron’s (Rashi: had you spoken to the rock, I would have been sanctified).

changes.before: I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star shall march out of Jacob, and a scepter shall rise from Israel. He shall crush Moab's temples and break down all the sons of Seth.
changes.after: I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star shall march out of Jacob, and a scepter shall rise from Israel. He shall crush the corners of Moab and break down all the sons of Seth.
changes.reason: Aloud, “Moab’s temples” suggests shrines; פַּאֲתֵי מוֹאָב is literally “the corners (sides) of Moab”, which Onkelos takes as Moab’s chiefs, so the literal wording is both clearer and closer to the source.

changes.before: Ships shall come from the coast of Kittim and afflict Asshur and Eber; but they too shall end in destruction.
changes.after: Ships shall come from the coast of Kittim and afflict Asshur and afflict Eber; but they too shall end in destruction.
changes.reason: The Hebrew repeats the verb (וְעִנּוּ אַשּׁוּר וְעִנּוּ־עֵבֶר); restoring the second “afflict” keeps the oracle’s parallel lines.

changes.before: Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned My wrath away from the sons of Israel by being zealous with My zeal among them, so that I did not consume the sons of Israel in My jealousy.
changes.after: Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned My wrath away from the sons of Israel by being zealous with My zeal among them, so that I did not consume the sons of Israel in My zeal.
changes.reason: קִנְאָתִי occurs twice in the verse, and rendering it “My zeal” both times keeps the deliberate echo: Phinehas was zealous with God’s zeal, so God’s zeal did not consume Israel (Rashi: he carried out My vengeance).

changes.before: because you rebelled against My command in the wilderness of Zin, during the congregation's dispute, concerning showing Me holy through the water before their eyes. These are the waters of Meribah at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.
changes.after: because you rebelled against My command in the wilderness of Zin, during the congregation's dispute, to show Me holy through the water before their eyes. These are the waters of Meribah at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.
changes.reason: לְהַקְדִּישֵׁנִי is a plain infinitive, which the column renders “to show Me holy” at 20:12; “concerning showing Me holy” is hard to follow aloud.

changes.before: You shall inherit the land by lot according to your clans. Give a larger inheritance to the larger group and a smaller inheritance to the smaller group. Wherever the lot falls for anyone shall be his. You shall inherit according to your ancestral tribes.
changes.after: You shall inherit the land by lot according to your clans. Give a larger inheritance to the larger group and a smaller inheritance to the smaller group. Wherever the lot falls for anyone, that shall be his. You shall inherit according to your ancestral tribes.
changes.reason: As read aloud the sentence has no subject; the Hebrew לוֹ יִהְיֶה (“it shall be his”) supplies one: wherever the lot falls, that place is his.

changes.before: Be careful lest you forget the covenant YHWH your God made with you and make yourselves a carved image in any form concerning which YHWH your God commanded you.
changes.after: Be careful lest you forget the covenant YHWH your God made with you and make yourselves a carved image in any form that YHWH your God has forbidden you.
changes.reason: אֲשֶׁר צִוְּךָ is elliptical and Rashi supplies “commanded you not to make”; “concerning which YHWH your God commanded you” can be heard as a command to make the image, and the column already renders the same construction “had forbidden” at 2:37.

changes.before: Because He loved your fathers, He chose his offspring after him and brought you out of Egypt in His presence, by His great power,
changes.after: Because He loved your fathers, He chose their offspring after them and brought you out of Egypt in His presence, by His great power,
changes.reason: The singular בְּזַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו refers to the fathers, but aloud “He chose his offspring after him” straight after “He” sounds like God’s offspring; the plural matches the column’s “their offspring after them” in the parallel 10:15.

changes.before: Rather, because YHWH loved you and kept the oath He swore to your fathers, YHWH brought you out with a mighty hand and redeemed you from the house of slaves, from Pharaoh king of Egypt's hand.
changes.after: Rather, because YHWH loved you and kept the oath He swore to your fathers, YHWH brought you out with a mighty hand and redeemed you from the house of slaves, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
changes.reason: “From Pharaoh king of Egypt’s hand” is heard aloud as “Egypt’s hand”; “from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt” follows the Hebrew order מִיַּד פַּרְעֹה מֶלֶךְ־מִצְרָיִם.

changes.before: going to serve other gods and bow down to them, to the sun, moon, or any of heaven's host, which I have not commanded,
changes.after: who has gone and served other gods and bowed down to them, to the sun, moon, or any of heaven's host, which I have not commanded,
changes.reason: וַיֵּלֶךְ וַיַּעֲבֹד … וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ state completed acts (he went, served and bowed down), but “going to serve” can be heard aloud as a mere intention.

changes.before: YHWH will hand your enemies who rise against you over defeated before you. They will come against you by one road and flee before you by seven roads.
changes.after: YHWH will hand over your enemies who rise against you, defeated before you. They will come against you by one road and flee before you by seven roads.
changes.reason: “Hand your enemies who rise against you over defeated” splits the verb from “over” across a clause and trips the ear; moving “over” keeps the column’s wording and its mirror with 28:25 (“give you over defeated”).

changes.before: YHWH will give you abundant good in the fruit of your womb, your livestock, and your ground, on the land YHWH swore to your fathers to give you.
changes.after: YHWH will give you abundant good in the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your livestock, and the fruit of your ground, on the land YHWH swore to your fathers to give you.
changes.reason: The Hebrew repeats בִּפְרִי (“in the fruit”) before womb, livestock and ground; restoring it keeps the refrain the column already keeps in 28:4 and 30:9.

changes.before: Cursed shall be the fruit of your womb and your ground, the increase of your cattle and the young of your flock.
changes.after: Cursed shall be the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground, the increase of your cattle and the young of your flock.
changes.reason: The Hebrew repeats פְּרִי (“fruit”) exactly as in the matching blessing of 28:4; restoring it keeps the curse a word-for-word mirror of the blessing.

changes.before: YHWH your God will put all these curses upon your enemies and those who hate and pursued you.
changes.after: YHWH your God will put all these curses upon your enemies and those who hate you, who pursued you.
changes.reason: “Those who hate and pursued you” joins two tenses on one object and sounds ungrammatical aloud; the Hebrew has “those who hate you, who pursued you” (שֹׂנְאֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר רְדָפוּךָ).

changes.before: He found him in a wilderness land, in a desolate, howling waste. He encircled him, cared for him, and guarded him like the pupil of His eye.
changes.after: He found him in a wilderness land, in a desolate, howling waste. He encircled him, instructed him, and guarded him like the pupil of His eye.
changes.reason: יְבוֹנְנֵהוּ is from בִּין, “understand”: He gave him understanding (Rashi: at Sinai He taught them Torah; Onkelos: “He taught them the words of His Torah”), and “cared for” loses the image of teaching.

changes.before: He said, “No; I have now come as commander of YHWH’s army.” Joshua fell on his face to the earth and bowed down. He said to him, “What does my lord say to his servant?”
changes.after: He said, “No; I am the commander of YHWH’s army. Now I have come.” Joshua fell on his face to the earth and bowed down. He said to him, “What does my lord say to his servant?”
changes.reason: The Hebrew makes two statements, אֲנִי שַׂר־צְבָא־יְהוָה (“I am the commander of YHWH’s army”) and עַתָּה בָאתִי (“now I have come”), which Rashi, following Megillah 3a, reads on its own as the reason for the visit; folding them into “come as commander” loses the self-identification.

changes.before: Israel has sinned. They have also transgressed My covenant that I commanded them. They have taken what was under the ban, stolen, lied, and put it among their own belongings.
changes.after: Israel has sinned. They have also transgressed My covenant that I commanded them; they have also taken what was under the ban; they have also stolen; they have also lied; and they have also put it among their own belongings.
changes.reason: The Hebrew repeats וְגַם (“and also”) five times, a deliberate piling-up of charges that the Talmud notes (Sanhedrin 44a); the English kept it only once and flattened the last four acts into a list.

changes.before: All Israel, its elders, officers, and judges stood on either side of the ark, opposite the Levitical priests carrying the ark of the covenant of YHWH, resident alien and native alike: half facing Mount Gerizim and half facing Mount Ebal, as Moses, the servant of YHWH, had first commanded them to bless the people of Israel.
changes.after: All Israel, its elders, officers, and judges stood on either side of the ark, opposite the Levitical priests carrying the ark of the covenant of YHWH, resident alien and native alike: half facing Mount Gerizim and half facing Mount Ebal, as Moses, the servant of YHWH, had commanded, to bless the people of Israel first.
changes.reason: בָּרִאשֹׁנָה is ambiguous; Rashi attaches it to the blessing (the blessing was pronounced first and then the curse, as in Mishnah Sotah 7:5 and 8:34 here), not to an earlier command of Moses.

changes.before: They cried to YHWH, and He placed darkness between you and the Egyptians, brought the sea over him and covered him. Your eyes saw what I did in Egypt. You lived in the wilderness many days.
changes.after: They cried to YHWH, and He placed darkness between you and the Egyptians, brought the sea over them and covered them. Your eyes saw what I did in Egypt. You lived in the wilderness many days.
changes.reason: עָלָיו and וַיְכַסֵּהוּ refer to Egypt as a collective; right after “the Egyptians”, “him” sounds aloud like an unnamed single person.

changes.before: So I have said, ‘I will not drive them out before you. They shall be adversaries at your sides, and their gods shall become a snare to you.’”
changes.after: And I also said, ‘I will not drive them out before you. They shall be adversaries at your sides, and their gods shall become a snare to you.’”
changes.reason: וְגַם אָמַרְתִּי is “and I also said”; Rashi reads it as the earlier warning (Num 33:55) now coming true, whereas “So I have said” makes it a new decree.

changes.before: Gideon and the hundred men with him came to the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, just as they had set the guards. They sounded the horns and smashed the jars in their hands.
changes.after: Gideon and the hundred men with him came to the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, when they had just set the guards. They sounded the horns and smashed the jars in their hands.
changes.reason: אַךְ הָקֵם הֵקִימוּ means the guards had only just been posted; “just as they had” can be heard as a comparison (“in the same way as”).

changes.before: He said to Zebah and Zalmunna, “Where are the men you killed at Tabor?” They said, “As you are, so were they; each had the appearance of a king’s sons.”
changes.after: He said to Zebah and Zalmunna, “What were the men like whom you killed at Tabor?” They said, “As you are, so were they; each had the appearance of a king’s sons.”
changes.reason: Here אֵיפֹה asks “of what kind” (Radak; Metzudat David), which is what the kings’ reply “As you are, so were they” answers; “Where are the men” makes the reply a non sequitur.

changes.before: He had thirty sons. He sent thirty daughters outside and brought thirty daughters from outside for his sons. He judged Israel for seven years.
changes.after: He had thirty sons, and thirty daughters whom he sent outside, and he brought thirty daughters from outside for his sons. He judged Israel for seven years.
changes.reason: The Hebrew says Ibzan had thirty sons and thirty daughters (וּשְׁלֹשִׁים בָּנוֹת שִׁלַּח הַחוּצָה); the English dropped that the daughters were his own, which the contrast with the thirty daughters brought in depends on.

changes.before: In those days there was no king in Israel. Each did what was right in his own eyes.
changes.after: In those days there was no king in Israel. Everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
changes.reason: The Hebrew refrain אִישׁ הַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינָיו יַעֲשֶׂה is identical here and at 21:25, where the column has “Everyone did what was right in his own eyes”; matching the wording keeps the book’s deliberate framing repetition.

changes.before: We have straw and fodder for our donkeys, and bread and wine for me, your maidservant, and the young man with your servants. We lack nothing.”
changes.after: We have straw and fodder for our donkeys, and bread and wine for me and for your maidservant and for the young man with your servants. We lack nothing.”
changes.reason: Aloud, “for me, your maidservant” sounds as if the Levite calls himself the maidservant; the Hebrew lists three parties with a repeated preposition (לִי וְלַאֲמָתֶךָ וְלַנַּעַר), which restoring “and for” makes clear.

changes.before: Now this is what we will do to Gibeah: against it by lot!
changes.after: Now this is what we will do to Gibeah: we will go up against it by lot.
changes.reason: The elliptical עָלֶיהָ בְּגוֹרָל is hard to follow aloud; Rashi and Targum Jonathan both supply “we will go up against it by lot”, and the verb is the one used for the attack in 20:18.

changes.before: The rising cloud began to ascend from the city, a pillar of smoke. Benjamin turned behind them, and look, the whole city was rising to heaven.
changes.after: The rising cloud began to ascend from the city, a pillar of smoke. Benjamin turned to see behind him, and look, the whole city was rising to heaven.
changes.reason: In וַיִּפֶן בִּנְיָמִן אַחֲרָיו the suffix is singular and refers to Benjamin, who turns to look back; “turned behind them” is unclear aloud and suggests Benjamin moved behind the Israelites.

changes.before: and thrust it into the basin, kettle, cauldron, or pot. Whatever the fork brought up, the priest took with it. This is what they did to all Israel who came there to Shiloh.
changes.after: and thrust it into the basin, or the kettle, or the cauldron, or the pot. Whatever the fork brought up, the priest took with it. This is what they did to all Israel who came there to Shiloh.
changes.reason: The Hebrew repeats אוֹ (“or”) before each vessel; restoring the repeated “or” keeps the source’s list of every pot the fork was plunged into.

changes.before: The messenger answered and said, “Israel has fled before the Philistines. There has been a great slaughter among the people. Your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are also dead, and God’s ark has been captured.”
changes.after: The messenger answered and said, “Israel has fled before the Philistines, and there has also been a great slaughter among the people. Your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are also dead, and God’s ark has been captured.”
changes.reason: The messenger’s report piles up וְגַם … וְגַם (“and also … and also”); restoring the first “also” keeps the mounting blow-by-blow news that the English kept only once.

changes.before: He will appoint for himself commanders of thousands and commanders of fifties, and set them to plow his plowing, reap his harvest, and make his weapons of war and his chariot equipment.
changes.after: He will appoint them for himself as commanders of thousands and commanders of fifties, and set them to plow his plowing, reap his harvest, and make his weapons of war and his chariot equipment.
changes.reason: The infinitives continue “he will take your sons” from v. 11: the sons are made commanders and plowmen; as written, the commanders themselves seemed to be set to plow.

changes.before: The Hebrews who had previously been with the Philistines and had gone up with them into the camp around also joined Israel with Saul and Jonathan.
changes.after: The Hebrews who had previously been with the Philistines and had gone up with them into the camp from all around also joined Israel with Saul and Jonathan.
changes.reason: סָבִיב means they had come up from the surrounding area (Radak); the bare “around” at the end of the phrase is hard to follow aloud.

changes.before: Samuel did what YHWH had spoken and came to Bethlehem. The city’s elders trembled as they met him, and he said, “Do you come in peace?”
changes.after: Samuel did what YHWH had spoken and came to Bethlehem. The city’s elders trembled as they met him and said, “Do you come in peace?”
changes.reason: The question is the elders’ (one speaking for them); “and he said” sounds aloud as if Samuel asked it.

changes.before: YHWH said to Samuel, “Do not look at his appearance or the height of his stature, for I have rejected him. I do not see as a human sees: a human looks at the eyes, but YHWH looks at the heart.”
changes.after: YHWH said to Samuel, “Do not look at his appearance or the height of his stature, for I have rejected him. I do not see as a human sees: a human looks at what meets the eyes, but YHWH looks at the heart.”
changes.reason: לַעֵינַיִם means what is visible to the eyes (Targum and Rashi: outward appearance); “looks at the eyes” sounds like looking into someone’s eyes.

changes.before: Samuel said to Jesse, “Are these all the young men?” He said, “The youngest still remains; he is tending the sheep.” Samuel said to Jesse, “Send and fetch him, for we will not sit around until he comes here.”
changes.after: Samuel said to Jesse, “Are these all the young men?” He said, “The youngest still remains; he is tending the sheep.” Samuel said to Jesse, “Send and fetch him, for we will not sit down at the table until he comes here.”
changes.reason: לֹא נָסֹב is reclining around the table for the sacrificial meal (Rashi); in English “sit around” means to idle.

changes.before: Saul kept watching David from that day onward.
changes.after: Saul eyed David with suspicion from that day onward.
changes.reason: The qere עוֹיֵן is hostile eyeing (Targum: lying in wait for David); “kept watching” loses the suspicion that the verse records.

changes.before: Saul sought to strike David and the wall with the spear, but he slipped away from Saul, and Saul drove the spear into the wall. David fled and escaped that night.
changes.after: Saul sought to pin David to the wall with the spear, but he slipped away from Saul, and Saul drove the spear into the wall. David fled and escaped that night.
changes.reason: “To strike with the spear into David and into the wall” means to pin him to the wall (Radak); “strike David and the wall” sounds as if the wall were a second target.

changes.before: He too stripped off his garments and prophesied before Samuel. He fell naked all that day and all the night. Therefore they say, “Is Saul also among the prophets?”
changes.after: He too stripped off his garments and prophesied before Samuel. He lay down naked all that day and all the night. Therefore they say, “Is Saul also among the prophets?”
changes.reason: וַיִּפֹּל here is falling down and lying there through the day and night; “fell … all that day” trips the ear.

changes.before: Then I will send the boy, saying, ‘Go, find the arrows.’ If I say to the boy, ‘Look, the arrows are on this side of you,’ take him and come, for there is peace for you and no danger, as YHWH lives.
changes.after: Then I will send the boy, saying, ‘Go, find the arrows.’ If I say to the boy, ‘Look, the arrows are on this side of you; take them,’ then come, for there is peace for you and no danger, as YHWH lives.
changes.reason: קָחֶנּוּ (“take it”) belongs to Jonathan’s words to the boy and refers to the arrows, after which David is to come; the English made it “take him” addressed to David.

changes.before: The boy went, and David rose from beside the south. He fell face down to the ground and bowed three times. They kissed one another and wept with one another, until David exceeded.
changes.after: The boy went, and David rose from beside the south side. He fell face down to the ground and bowed three times. They kissed one another and wept with one another, until David wept the more.
changes.reason: Two unclear phrases made plain with Rashi: מֵאֵצֶל הַנֶּגֶב is the spot on the south side (of the stone), and עַד־דָּוִד הִגְדִּיל means David’s weeping exceeded Jonathan’s, which “until David exceeded” does not say.

changes.before: David said, “YHWH, God of Israel, Your servant has heard that Saul seeks to come to Keilah and destroy the city because of me.
changes.after: David said, “YHWH, God of Israel, Your servant has surely heard that Saul seeks to come to Keilah and destroy the city because of me.
changes.reason: The Hebrew doubles the verb (שָׁמֹעַ שָׁמַע) for certainty, which the column elsewhere renders with “surely”; restoring it keeps David’s emphasis.

changes.before: He sent it to those in Bethel, Ramoth-negeb and Jattir;
changes.after: He sent it to those in Bethel, to those in Ramoth-negeb, and to those in Jattir;
changes.reason: The Hebrew repeats לַאֲשֶׁר (“to those in”) before every town in this roll call; restoring the repetition keeps the list’s deliberate cadence.

changes.before: to those in Aroer, Siphmoth and Eshtemoa;
changes.after: to those in Aroer, to those in Siphmoth, and to those in Eshtemoa;
changes.reason: As in 30:27, the Hebrew repeats לַאֲשֶׁר before each town; the repeated “to those in” restores the roll-call pattern.

changes.before: to those in Racal, the cities of the Jerahmeelites, and the cities of the Kenites;
changes.after: to those in Racal, to those in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, and to those in the cities of the Kenites;
changes.reason: As in 30:27, the Hebrew repeats לַאֲשֶׁר before each place; the repeated “to those in” restores the roll-call pattern.

changes.before: to those in Hormah, Bor-ashan and Athach;
changes.after: to those in Hormah, to those in Bor-ashan, and to those in Athach;
changes.reason: As in 30:27, the Hebrew repeats לַאֲשֶׁר before each town; the repeated “to those in” restores the roll-call pattern.

changes.before: Nevertheless, because by this deed you have utterly despised YHWH’s enemies, the son born to you will certainly die.”
changes.after: Nevertheless, because by this deed you have surely given YHWH’s enemies cause to scorn, the son born to you will certainly die.”
changes.reason: “Scorned YHWH’s enemies” is a euphemism for scorning YHWH; following Targum Jonathan (David caused YHWH’s enemies to blaspheme), the English no longer sounds as if David despised the enemies.

changes.before: Absalom instructed his young men, “Watch when Amnon’s heart is merry with wine. When I say to you, ‘Strike Amnon,’ kill him. Do not be afraid. Have I not commanded you? Be strong and be valiant men.”
changes.after: Absalom instructed his young men, “Watch when Amnon’s heart is merry with wine. When I say to you, ‘Strike Amnon,’ kill him. Do not be afraid. Is it not I who have commanded you? Be strong and be valiant men.”
changes.reason: The emphatic אָנֹכִי stresses that Absalom himself takes responsibility for the order; the plain question loses that stress.

changes.before: That is not the matter. A man from the hill country of Ephraim, named Sheba son of Bichri, has raised his hand against the king, against David. Give up him alone, and I will withdraw from the city.” The woman said to Joab, “His head will be thrown to you over the wall.”
changes.after: That is not the matter. A man from the hill country of Ephraim, named Sheba son of Bichri, has raised his hand against the king, against David. Give him up, him alone, and I will withdraw from the city.” The woman said to Joab, “His head will be thrown to you over the wall.”
changes.reason: “Give up him alone” trips the ear; the rewording keeps לְבַדּוֹ (“him alone”) in natural word order.

changes.before: The king took Rizpah daughter of Aiah’s two sons whom she bore to Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth, and Michal daughter of Saul’s five sons whom she bore to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite.
changes.after: The king took the two sons of Rizpah daughter of Aiah, whom she bore to Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth, and the five sons of Michal daughter of Saul, whom she bore to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite.
changes.reason: The stacked possessives (“Michal daughter of Saul’s five sons”) sound aloud as if the sons were Saul’s; “the sons of …” follows the Hebrew order and is clear.

changes.before: They buried the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan in Benjamin’s land, at Zela, in the tomb of Saul’s father Kish. They did everything the king commanded. Afterward God answered entreaty for the land.
changes.after: They buried the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan in Benjamin’s land, at Zela, in the tomb of Saul’s father Kish. They did everything the king commanded. Afterward God heeded the plea for the land.
changes.reason: “Answered entreaty” without an article is hard to follow aloud; וַיֵּעָתֵר means God let Himself be entreated, i.e. heeded the plea.

changes.before: Ishbi-benob, one of Rapha’s descendants, had a spear weighing three hundred in weight of bronze and was belted with a new weapon. He intended to strike David down.
changes.after: Ishbi-benob, one of Rapha’s descendants, had a spear weighing three hundred shekels of bronze and was belted with a new weapon. He intended to strike David down.
changes.reason: “Three hundred in weight of bronze” is unintelligible aloud; the unit implied by מִשְׁקַל is the shekel (as the commentators supply).

changes.before: He made darkness booths around Him: gathered waters, thick clouds of the skies.
changes.after: He set darkness around Him as booths: gathered waters, thick clouds of the skies.
changes.reason: “Darkness booths” sounds like a compound noun; the Hebrew sets darkness around Him as booths (canopies).

changes.before: He sent arrows and scattered them, lightning and threw them into confusion.
changes.after: He sent arrows and scattered them; He sent lightning and threw them into confusion.
changes.reason: “Lightning and threw them into confusion” has no verb for lightning when heard; the Hebrew’s “He sent” governs both arrows and lightning, so it is supplied.

changes.before: When David saw the angel striking the people, he spoke to YHWH and said, “Look, I have sinned; I have done wrong. But these sheep—what have they done? Please let Your hand be against me and my father’s house.”
changes.after: When David saw the angel striking the people, he spoke to YHWH and said, “Look, it is I who have sinned, and I who have done wrong. But these sheep—what have they done? Please let Your hand be against me and my father’s house.”
changes.reason: The repeated emphatic אָנֹכִי (“I … and I”) sets David against “these sheep”; the plain verbs lose that deliberate contrast.

changes.before: David built an altar to YHWH there and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. YHWH answered entreaty for the land, and the plague was restrained from Israel.
changes.after: David built an altar to YHWH there and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. YHWH heeded the plea for the land, and the plague was restrained from Israel.
changes.reason: As in 21:14, “answered entreaty” is hard to follow aloud; וַיֵּעָתֵר means YHWH heeded the plea.

changes.before: You also know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me, what he did to the two commanders of Israel’s armies, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether. He killed them, bringing the blood of war into peace, and put the blood of war on the belt around his waist and the sandal on his feet.
changes.after: You also know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me, what he did to the two commanders of Israel’s armies, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether. He killed them, shedding the blood of war in peacetime, and put the blood of war on the belt around his waist and the sandal on his feet.
changes.reason: וַיָּשֶׂם דְּמֵי־מִלְחָמָה בְּשָׁלֹם means he shed war-blood in a time of peace (so Rashi); “bringing … into peace” is unclear when heard.

changes.before: The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high. He overlaid it with pure gold and covered the altar with cedar.
changes.after: The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high. He overlaid it with pure gold, and he overlaid the cedar altar.
changes.reason: וַיְצַף מִזְבֵּחַ אָרֶז is read by Targum, Rashi and Radak as overlaying the cedar altar (with gold, cf. 6:22), not covering an altar with cedar.

changes.before: This house shall be conspicuous: everyone passing by it will be appalled and hiss, saying, ‘Why has YHWH done this to this land and this house?’
changes.after: And this house, which was so exalted—everyone passing by it will be appalled and hiss, saying, ‘Why has YHWH done this to this land and this house?’
changes.reason: With Targum and Rashi, עֶלְיוֹן describes the house as once exalted (now desolate), not as becoming “conspicuous”.

changes.before: The king took counsel and made two golden calves. He said to them, “You have gone up to Jerusalem long enough. Look, your gods, Israel, who brought you up from Egypt!”
changes.after: The king took counsel and made two golden calves. He said to them, “You have gone up to Jerusalem long enough. Look, your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt!”
changes.reason: The Hebrew has “from the land of Egypt” (מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם), the exact wording of the golden-calf cry in Exodus 32:4, 8, which the verse deliberately echoes.

changes.before: “There is a covenant between me and you, between my father and your father. Look, I have sent you a gift of silver and gold. Go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, so he will withdraw from me.”
changes.after: “There is a covenant between me and you, between my father and your father. Look, I have sent you a bribe of silver and gold. Go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, so he will withdraw from me.”
changes.reason: שֹׁחַד is the Hebrew word for a bribe, not a neutral gift; the source names Asa’s payment for what it is.

changes.before: Has my lord not been told what I did when Jezebel was killing YHWH’s prophets—how I hid a hundred men from YHWH’s prophets, fifty men to a cave, and sustained them with bread and water?
changes.after: Has my lord not been told what I did when Jezebel was killing YHWH’s prophets—how I hid a hundred men of YHWH’s prophets, fifty men to a cave, and sustained them with bread and water?
changes.reason: Aloud, “hid a hundred men from YHWH’s prophets” sounds as if he hid them from the prophets; the Hebrew מִנְּבִיאֵי means a hundred of the prophets themselves.

changes.before: The sons of the prophets at Jericho saw him from opposite him and said, ‘The spirit of Elijah has rested upon Elisha.’ They came to meet him and bowed to the ground before him.
changes.after: The sons of the prophets at Jericho, watching from opposite, saw him and said, ‘The spirit of Elijah has rested upon Elisha.’ They came to meet him and bowed to the ground before him.
changes.reason: “Saw him from opposite him” trips the ear; the rewording keeps מִנֶּגֶד (from opposite, where they stood in 2:7) without the doubled “him”.

changes.before: Elisha said to him, ‘Go, say: You will certainly not live. YHWH has shown me that he will surely die.’
changes.after: Elisha said to him, ‘Go, say to him: You will surely live. But YHWH has shown me that he will surely die.’
changes.reason: Follows the Qere לוֹ (“to him”) over the Ketiv לֹא (“not”), as Targum and Rashi do (he would recover from the illness yet die by other means); Hazael’s report in 8:14 confirms “You will surely live.”

changes.before: He fixed his face and held it until there was shame, and the man of God wept.
changes.after: He fixed his face and held it until he was ashamed, and the man of God wept.
changes.reason: עַד־בֹּשׁ means “until he was ashamed” (Rashi: the fixed stare went on until shame set in); “until there was shame” is hard to follow aloud.

changes.before: Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Jehoash son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh. They came to Jerusalem, and he broke through Jerusalem's wall from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.
changes.after: Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Jehoash son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh. He came to Jerusalem and broke through Jerusalem's wall from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.
changes.reason: Follows the Qere וַיָּבֹא (“he came”), so Jehoash is the one who comes and breaches the wall, in line with the singular verbs around it.

changes.before: For YHWH saw Israel's affliction was very bitter: none remained confined and none remained free, and Israel had no helper.
changes.after: For YHWH saw that Israel's affliction was very bitter: none remained confined and none remained free, and Israel had no helper.
changes.reason: Without “that” the listener first hears “YHWH saw Israel’s affliction” as a complete clause and then stumbles on “was very bitter.”

changes.before: At that time Rezin king of Aram restored Elath to Aram and drove the Judeans out of Eloth. Arameans came to Elath and lived there to this day.
changes.after: At that time Rezin king of Aram restored Elath to Aram and drove the Judeans out of Eloth. Edomites came to Elath and lived there to this day.
changes.reason: The Masoretic Qere reads וַאֲדוֹמִים (“Edomites”) for the Ketiv וארמים; the column follows the Qere, and the Edomites’ settling in Elath is the point of the verse.

changes.before: The king of Assyria discovered a conspiracy in Hoshea: he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt and had not brought tribute to the king of Assyria as year after year. The king of Assyria detained him and bound him in prison.
changes.after: The king of Assyria discovered a conspiracy in Hoshea: he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt and had not brought tribute to the king of Assyria as he had done year by year. The king of Assyria detained him and bound him in prison.
changes.reason: כְּשָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה means “as (he had paid) year by year”; “as year after year” is not a complete thought when read aloud.

changes.before: They captured it at the end of three years. In Hezekiah's sixth year, which was Hoshea king of Israel's ninth year, Samaria was captured.
changes.after: They captured it at the end of three years. In Hezekiah's sixth year, which was the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria was captured.
changes.reason: The stacked possessive “Hoshea king of Israel’s ninth year” trips the ear; this matches the wording of 18:9.

changes.before: For a remnant shall come out from Jerusalem, and survivors from Mount Zion. YHWH's zeal shall do this.
changes.after: For a remnant shall come out from Jerusalem, and survivors from Mount Zion. The zeal of YHWH of hosts shall do this.
changes.reason: The qere adds צְבָאוֹת (read though not written), so the reading tradition has “the zeal of YHWH of hosts”, as in Isaiah 37:32.

changes.before: As he was bowing down in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him with the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. His son Esarhaddon became king in his place.
changes.after: As he was bowing down in the house of Nisroch his god, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him with the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. His son Esarhaddon became king in his place.
changes.reason: The qere supplies בָּנָיו (“his sons”), read though not written; following the Masoretic reading restores that the assassins were his own sons.

changes.before: Before Isaiah had gone out of the middle city, YHWH's word came to him:
changes.after: Before Isaiah had gone out of the middle court, YHWH's word came to him:
changes.reason: The ketiv has הָעִיר (“city”) but the qere is חָצֵר (“court”), and the Targum follows the qere: Isaiah had not yet left the middle court of the palace.

changes.before: He put an end to the kemarim whom Judah's kings had appointed—and he burned offerings at the high places in Judah's cities and around Jerusalem—and to those burning offerings to Baal, the sun, the moon, the constellations, and all heaven's host.
changes.after: He put an end to the kemarim whom Judah's kings had appointed, who burned offerings at the high places in Judah's cities and around Jerusalem, and to those burning offerings to Baal, the sun, the moon, the constellations, and all heaven's host.
changes.reason: וַיְקַטֵּר refers to the kemarim (Targum renders “who were burning incense”; Radak: each of them), but “and he burned offerings” makes it sound as if Josiah burned offerings at the high places.

changes.before: He defiled Topheth in the valley of the sons of Hinnom, so that no one would pass his son or daughter through fire to Molech.
changes.after: He defiled Topheth in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, so that no one would pass his son or daughter through fire to Molech.
changes.reason: The qere is בֶן־הִנֹּם (“son of Hinnom”), not the ketiv “sons”; the column elsewhere writes “the Valley of the Son of Hinnom” (Joshua 15:8, Jeremiah 19:2).

changes.before: Pharaoh Neco bound him at Riblah in Hamath's land while he was reigning in Jerusalem. He imposed a penalty on the land of one hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.
changes.after: Pharaoh Neco bound him at Riblah in Hamath's land so that he would not reign in Jerusalem. He imposed a penalty on the land of one hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.
changes.reason: The qere מִמְּלֹךְ means “from reigning” (Targum: from being king); “while he was reigning” follows the ketiv בִּמְלֹךְ and loses the point that Neco deposed him.

changes.before: Keturah's sons, Abraham's concubine: she bore Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. Jokshan's sons: Sheba and Dedan.
changes.after: The sons of Keturah, Abraham's concubine: she bore Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. Jokshan's sons: Sheba and Dedan.
changes.reason: Read aloud, “Keturah's sons, Abraham's concubine” makes the sons the concubine; “the sons of Keturah, Abraham's concubine” keeps the apposition on Keturah, as in the Hebrew.

changes.before: Caleb son of Hezron fathered Azubah-ishah and Jerioth. These were her sons: Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
changes.after: Caleb son of Hezron fathered children by Azubah, a wife, and by Jerioth. These were her sons: Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
changes.reason: אִשָּׁה is “a wife”, not part of a name, and the את marks the mothers by whom Caleb fathered children (Radak reads it as “from”), so “fathered Azubah-ishah” invents a name and makes the wives his daughters.

changes.before: They lodged around the house of God because the guard duty rested on them; they were responsible for opening it morning by morning.
changes.after: They lodged around the house of God because the guard duty rested on them; they were over the key, to open it morning by morning.
changes.reason: The Hebrew says they were “over the key” (עַל־הַמַּפְתֵּחַ); restoring the key keeps the source’s concrete image of their charge.

changes.before: Even formerly, when Saul was king, you were the one who led Israel out and brought them in. YHWH your God said to you, ‘You shall shepherd My people Israel, and you shall be leader over My people Israel.’”
changes.after: Even in times past, even when Saul was king, you were the one who led Israel out and brought them in. YHWH your God said to you, ‘You shall shepherd My people Israel, and you shall be leader over My people Israel.’”
changes.reason: The Hebrew repeats גַּם (“even … even”) through the idiom “yesterday and the day before”; restoring the repeated “even” keeps the elders’ emphatic build-up.

changes.before: Benaiah son of Jehoiada, son of a valiant man, accomplished many deeds, from Kabzeel. He struck the two ariels of Moab; he also went down and struck the lion in the pit on a snowy day.
changes.after: Benaiah son of Jehoiada, son of a valiant man of many deeds from Kabzeel—he struck the two ariels of Moab; he also went down and struck the lion in the pit on a snowy day.
changes.reason: “Accomplished many deeds, from Kabzeel” leaves the hometown dangling aloud; following the Hebrew phrase order (בֶּן־אִישׁ־חַיִל רַב־פְּעָלִים מִן־קַבְצְאֵל, then הוּא הִכָּה) reads cleanly.

changes.before: Because you were not there the first time, YHWH our God broke out against us, for we did not seek Him according to the rule.”
changes.after: Because the first time it was not you who carried it, YHWH our God broke out against us, for we did not seek Him according to the rule.”
changes.reason: לֹא אַתֶּם means “it was not you” doing it, not that they were absent; Rashi explains that the Levites did not carry the ark the first time, it went on a cart.

changes.before: He distributed to every Israelite, man and woman alike, to each a loaf of bread, an eshpar, and a raisin cake.
changes.after: He distributed to every Israelite, man and woman alike, to each a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a raisin cake.
changes.reason: The transliteration “eshpar” cannot be followed aloud; Rashi explains אֶשְׁפָּר as a portion of meat (one sixth of a bull).

changes.before: David said to Solomon his son, “As for me, it was in my heart to build a house for the name of YHWH my God.
changes.after: David said to Solomon, “My son, as for me, it was in my heart to build a house for the name of YHWH my God.
changes.reason: The English follows the written form בנו (“his son”); the Masoretic reading (qere) is בְּנִי, “my son”, David’s address to Solomon, as the column follows the qere elsewhere.

changes.before: YHWH, the God of Israel, chose me from all my father's house to be king over Israel forever. He chose Judah as leader, and in Judah's house my father's house, and among my father's sons He was pleased with me to make me king over all Israel.
changes.after: YHWH, the God of Israel, chose me from all my father's house to be king over Israel forever. For He chose Judah as leader, and in Judah's house my father's house, and among my father's sons He was pleased with me to make me king over all Israel.
changes.reason: The Hebrew opens this clause with כִּי (“for”): David explains his own choice by God’s choice of Judah, and the dropped “for” loses that reasoning.

changes.before: [BHS 1:6] Solomon offered there upon the bronze altar before YHWH, which belonged to the Tent of Meeting; he offered a thousand burnt offerings upon it.
changes.after: [BHS 1:6] Solomon offered there before YHWH upon the bronze altar that belonged to the Tent of Meeting; he offered a thousand burnt offerings upon it.
changes.reason: Heard aloud, “before YHWH, which belonged to the Tent of Meeting” attaches the clause to YHWH; it describes the altar, so the phrases are reordered.

changes.before: [BHS 1:13] Solomon came to the high place that was in Gibeon, to Jerusalem, from before the Tent of Meeting, and he reigned over Israel.
changes.after: [BHS 1:13] Solomon came from the high place that was in Gibeon to Jerusalem, from before the Tent of Meeting, and he reigned over Israel.
changes.reason: Solomon is returning from Gibeon to Jerusalem (“from before the Tent of Meeting”); Rashi and Radak read לַבָּמָה here as “from the high place”, where “came to” sends him the wrong way.

changes.before: [BHS 3:15] He made two pillars before the house, thirty-five cubits in length, with the capital upon its top five cubits.
changes.after: [BHS 3:15] He made two pillars before the house, thirty-five cubits in length, and the capital upon its top was five cubits.
changes.reason: “With the capital upon its top five cubits” is hard to follow aloud; a plain clause states the capital’s height.

changes.before: [BHS 4:11] Huram made the pots, shovels, and sprinkling basins. Hiram finished doing the work he did for King Solomon in God's house:
changes.after: [BHS 4:11] Huram made the pots, shovels, and sprinkling basins. Huram finished doing the work he did for King Solomon in God's house:
changes.reason: The qere (the reading tradition) is חוּרָם, Huram, as earlier in this verse and throughout the column’s Chronicles; “Hiram” follows the ketiv and sounds like a different man.

changes.before: [BHS 9:10] The servants of Hiram and Solomon’s servants, who brought gold from Ophir, also brought algum wood and precious stones.
changes.after: [BHS 9:10] The servants of Huram and Solomon’s servants, who brought gold from Ophir, also brought algum wood and precious stones.
changes.reason: The qere is חוּרָם, Huram, the spelling the column uses for this king in Chronicles (e.g. 8:18, 9:21); “Hiram” follows the ketiv.

changes.before: [BHS 9:29] The rest of Solomon’s deeds, first and last—are they not written in the records of Nathan the prophet, the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and the visions of Jeddoi the seer concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat?
changes.after: [BHS 9:29] The rest of Solomon’s deeds, first and last—are they not written in the records of Nathan the prophet, the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat?
changes.reason: “Jeddoi” matches neither the ketiv יעדי nor the qere יֶעְדּוֹ; tradition identifies this seer with Iddo, as the column names him in 12:15 and 13:22.

changes.before: [BHS 11:18] Rehoboam took as wife Mahalath, daughter of Jerimoth son of David, and Abihail daughter of Eliab son of Jesse.
changes.after: [BHS 11:18] Rehoboam took as wife Mahalath, daughter of Jerimoth son of David and of Abihail daughter of Eliab son of Jesse.
changes.reason: The Hebrew has no “and” before Abihail; with Rashi and Radak she is Mahalath’s mother, not a second wife (v. 19 “she bore him” and v. 20 “after her” speak of one wife).

changes.before: [BHS 18:33] A man drew his bow innocently and struck the king of Israel between the joints and the armor. The king said to the chariot driver, “Turn your hands and take me out of the camp, for I am wounded.”
changes.after: [BHS 18:33] A man drew his bow innocently and struck the king of Israel between the joints and the armor. The king said to the chariot driver, “Turn your hand and take me out of the camp, for I am wounded.”
changes.reason: The qere (followed by this column elsewhere) reads יָדְךָ “your hand” in the singular, the idiom for wheeling the chariot around, as in 1 Kings 22:34.

changes.before: [BHS 32:5] He strengthened himself, rebuilt the entire breached wall, and went up upon the towers; outside was another wall. He strengthened the Millo of the City of David and made weapons in abundance and shields.
changes.after: [BHS 32:5] He strengthened himself, rebuilt the entire breached wall, and raised it up to the towers; outside was another wall. He strengthened the Millo of the City of David and made weapons in abundance and shields.
changes.reason: וַיַּעַל here is causative (as in Gen 8:20); Rashi explains that he raised the wall up to the height of the towers, which “went up upon the towers” obscures.

changes.before: [BHS 34:6] And in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, as far as Naphtali, on the mountain of their houses all around,
changes.after: [BHS 34:6] And in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, as far as Naphtali, in their ruins all around,
changes.reason: The qere בְּחַרְבֹתֵיהֶם “in their ruins” (which the column follows elsewhere) replaces the ketiv בהר בתיהם, whose literal “on the mountain of their houses” is unintelligible aloud.

changes.before: [BHS 35:5] Stand in the holy place according to the divisions of the ancestral houses of your brothers, the people’s members, with an ancestral-house portion for the Levites.
changes.after: [BHS 35:5] Stand in the holy place according to the divisions of the ancestral houses of your brothers, the people, with an ancestral-house portion for the Levites.
changes.reason: בְּנֵי הָעָם means the lay people as distinct from the Levites; “the people’s members” trips the ear, and “the people” matches 35:7.

changes.before: [BHS 35:12] They set aside the burnt offering to give portions according to the divisions of the ancestral houses of the people’s members, to present to YHWH as written in the Book of Moses; they did likewise with the cattle.
changes.after: [BHS 35:12] They set aside the burnt offering to give portions according to the divisions of the ancestral houses of the people, to present to YHWH as written in the Book of Moses; they did likewise with the cattle.
changes.reason: As in 35:5, בְּנֵי הָעָם is simply the lay people; “the people’s members” is awkward when read aloud.

changes.before: [BHS 35:13] They cooked the Passover offering with fire according to the ordinance. They cooked the holy offerings in pots, cauldrons, and pans and hurried them to all the people’s members.
changes.after: [BHS 35:13] They cooked the Passover offering with fire according to the ordinance. They cooked the holy offerings in pots, cauldrons, and pans and hurried them to all the people.
changes.reason: As in 35:5, בְּנֵי הָעָם is simply the lay people; “the people’s members” is awkward when read aloud.

changes.before: They approached Zerubbabel and the heads of the ancestral houses and said to them, “Let us build with you, for like you we seek your God, and we have not been sacrificing since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us up here.”
changes.after: They approached Zerubbabel and the heads of the ancestral houses and said to them, “Let us build with you, for like you we seek your God, and we have been sacrificing to Him since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us up here.”
changes.reason: Follows the qere וְלוֹ (“and to Him”) over the ketiv ולא (“not”), as the column follows the qere elsewhere; the adversaries claim to have been sacrificing to Israel’s God, which is the point of their offer.

changes.before: All these had taken foreign wives; and among them were wives, and they placed sons.
changes.after: All these had taken foreign wives, and some of them had wives by whom they had sons.
changes.reason: וְיֵשׁ מֵהֶם נָשִׁים וַיָּשִׂימוּ בָּנִים means some had wives who had borne them sons; “they placed sons” is unintelligible when read aloud.

changes.before: Shallun son of Col-hozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate. He built it and roofed it, and they set up its doors, locks and bars, and the wall of the Pool of Shelah by the king's garden, as far as the steps descending from the City of David.
changes.after: Shallun son of Col-hozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate. He built it, roofed it and set up its doors, locks and bars, and the wall of the Pool of Shelah by the king's garden, as far as the steps descending from the City of David.
changes.reason: Follows the qere וְיַעֲמִיד (“and he set up”) over the ketiv plural, keeping Shallun as the one subject of the verse, as in 3:14.
