changes.before: After me Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired a second section. After him Meshullam son of Berechiah repaired opposite his chamber.
changes.after: After him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired a second section. After him Meshullam son of Berechiah repaired opposite his chamber.
changes.reason: Follows the qere אַחֲרָיו (“after him”) over the ketiv אחרי (“after me”); Nehemiah is not listed among the repairers, and the column follows the qere elsewhere.

changes.before: After me Malchijah, of the goldsmiths, repaired as far as the house of the Nethinim and the merchants, opposite the Muster Gate, and as far as the upper chamber of the corner.
changes.after: After him Malchijah, of the goldsmiths, repaired as far as the house of the Nethinim and the merchants, opposite the Muster Gate, and as far as the upper chamber of the corner.
changes.reason: Follows the qere אַחֲרָיו (“after him”) over the ketiv אחרי (“after me”), as in 3:30; the list proceeds section by section from the previous repairer.

changes.before: He said, “What you are doing is not good. Should you not walk in the fear of our God, to avoid the reproach of the nations, our enemies?
changes.after: I said, “What you are doing is not good. Should you not walk in the fear of our God, to avoid the reproach of the nations, our enemies?
changes.reason: Follows the qere וָאוֹמַר (“and I said”) over the ketiv ויאמר; Nehemiah is still the speaker rebuking the nobles, as in 5:7–8 and 5:10.

changes.before: He said to them, “The gates of Jerusalem must not be opened until the sun is hot. While they are still standing there, let them shut the doors and secure them. Appoint watches from the inhabitants of Jerusalem, each at his watch and each opposite his house.”
changes.after: I said to them, “The gates of Jerusalem must not be opened until the sun is hot. While they are still standing there, let them shut the doors and secure them. Appoint watches from the inhabitants of Jerusalem, each at his watch and each opposite his house.”
changes.reason: The Qere וָאֹמַר is first person, “I said” (Nehemiah giving the order, as Rashi reads it); the English made the speaker “he”.

changes.before: “You warned them to turn them back to Your law, but they acted arrogantly and did not listen to Your commandments. They sinned against Your judgments, which a person shall do and live by them. They presented a stubborn shoulder, stiffened their necks and did not listen.
changes.after: “You warned them to turn them back to Your law, but they acted arrogantly and did not listen to Your commandments. They sinned against Your judgments, which, if a person does them, he shall live by them. They presented a stubborn shoulder, stiffened their necks and did not listen.
changes.reason: The clause echoing Leviticus 18:5 (אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם וְחָיָה בָהֶם) was hard to follow aloud; recast as a conditional while keeping “live by them”.

changes.before: The two thanksgiving companies stood in the house of God, with me and half the officials with me,
changes.after: The two thanksgiving companies stood in the house of God, and so did I and half the officials with me,
changes.reason: וַאֲנִי וַחֲצִי הַסְּגָנִים עִמִּי makes Nehemiah a second subject who also stood; the doubled “with me” blurred that when read aloud.

changes.before: [BHS 3:6] He considered it beneath him to lay hands on Mordecai alone, for they had told him Mordecai’s people. Haman sought to destroy all the Jews throughout Ahasuerus’s kingdom, Mordecai’s people.
changes.after: [BHS 3:6] He considered it beneath him to lay hands on Mordecai alone, for they had told him who Mordecai’s people were. Haman sought to destroy all the Jews throughout Ahasuerus’s kingdom, Mordecai’s people.
changes.reason: הִגִּידוּ לוֹ אֶת־עַם מָרְדֳּכָי means they told him which people Mordecai belonged to; “told him Mordecai’s people” is unclear aloud.

changes.before: I have sinned—what have I done to You, Watcher of humanity? Why have You made me Your target, so that I am a burden to myself?
changes.after: If I have sinned, what do I do to You, Watcher of humanity? Why have You made me Your target, so that I am a burden to myself?
changes.reason: אֶפְעַל is imperfect (“what do I do”), not past; following Rashi, Job argues that even if he has sinned, it does God no harm.

changes.before: Are not my days few? Let Him cease; let Him turn away from me, so that I may brighten a little,
changes.after: Are not my days few? Cease, and turn away from me, so that I may brighten a little,
changes.reason: The qere וַחֲדָל וְשִׁית are imperatives addressed to God, matching Job’s direct “You” throughout the chapter; the third person followed the ketiv.

changes.before: Look, He may kill me; I have no hope. Yet I will argue my ways before Him.
changes.after: Look, He may kill me; I will hope in Him. Yet I will argue my ways before Him.
changes.reason: The qere לוֹ (“in Him”), followed by the Targum and Rashi, makes this a declaration of hope; the English followed the ketiv לֹא and reversed the meaning.

changes.before: If you say, ‘How we will pursue him!’ and, ‘The root of the matter is found in me,’
changes.after: If you say, ‘How shall we pursue him?’ and, ‘The root of the matter is found in me,’
changes.reason: מַה־נִּרְדָּף־לוֹ is a question (“how shall we pursue him?”, as Rashi reads it), not an exclamation; the exclamation makes the friends sound as if they boast of hounding Job.

changes.before: If you return to Shaddai, you will be built up; put wrongdoing far from your tents.
changes.after: If you return to Shaddai, you will be built up; put wrongdoing far from your tent.
changes.reason: מֵאָהֳלֶךָ is singular, “from your tent”.

changes.before: For I was not cut off before darkness, and He concealed gloom from my face.
changes.after: For I was not cut off before darkness, nor did He conceal gloom from my face.
changes.reason: The negative carries into the second line; Rashi reads it as Job’s complaint that God did not cut him off before the darkness nor hide the gloom from him, whereas the current English says God did conceal it.

changes.before: Coral and crystal are not worth mentioning; the drawing of wisdom is beyond precious stones.
changes.after: Coral and crystal are not worth mentioning; the acquiring of wisdom is beyond precious stones.
changes.reason: מֶשֶׁךְ חָכְמָה is the drawing-in, i.e. acquiring, of wisdom (so the classical commentators); “the drawing of wisdom” sounds aloud like a picture.

changes.before: For He loosened His cord and afflicted me, and they cast off the bridle before me.
changes.after: For He loosened my cord and afflicted me, and they cast off the bridle before me.
changes.reason: The Qere יִתְרִי reads “my cord”; the column follows the Qere elsewhere in this chunk (e.g. 21:20, 26:14, 31:20), and the English here followed the Ketiv.

changes.before: Can one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the righteous, mighty One?
changes.after: Can one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the righteous and mighty One?
changes.reason: צַדִּיק כַּבִּיר is the object, God as righteous and mighty; with only a comma, the listener hears “mighty One” as a vocative addressed to Job.
